Overview: The common cold is medically defined as a viral upper respiratory tract infection. Rhinoviruses account for up to two-fifths of cases of the common cold. The infection usually resolves within 7 to 10 days, making it a self-limiting condition. It can lead to complications such as bronchiolitis in immunocompromised individuals and exacerbation of existing pulmonary conditions like asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It thrives in cooler temperatures found in the nasal passages (around 33°C), which explains why it is often referred to as a "head cold"
Symptoms: Symptoms of a common common cold include runny nose (rhinorrhea) Sneezing Sore throat (cough) Dry throat, throat itch, or throat pain General malaise or not feeling well Other symptoms include low-grade fever (more common in children), headaches, and general body aches
Causes: Nasal sprays can reduce the duration and severity of the common cold.
Treatment: Symptomatic management of the common cold. Antibiotics are ineffective against viral infections and should not be used to treat common colds. Zinc lozenges, especially if initiated within 24 hours of symptom onset at doses of at least 75 mg/day of elemental zinc, have been shown to shorten the duration and severity of common cold symptoms, particularly severe symptoms, when taken in doses of at least 75 mg/day of elemental Zinc lozenges
When to See a Doctor: Most common common colds are mild and resolve on their own, but certain situations warrant a visit to the doctor
